record.narrative: Both validation results delivered for this synthesis stage fail to support the original stronger-dependency claims. For H23, outcome_006 feature_042 had a discovery signed mean difference of +0.0534, but the 95% discovery interval [0.0114, 0.0954] did not rule in the scale-aware 10% benchmark for outcome_006 (~0.0175). Independent validation R25 gives a signed difference of -0.0091 with independent interval [-0.0653, 0.0471], i.e., the validation estimate is opposite to the discovery claim. Although the independent interval does not exclude all clinically meaningful positive effects, the combined discovery-plus-validation pattern provides no supported clinically meaningful association, and feature_042 is already inconsistent across outcomes (notably outcome_008 opposite). I therefore keep H23 rejected and closed. For H26, outcome_008 feature_047 was the strongest remaining discovery candidate: signed difference +0.0282, interval [0.0019, 0.0546], point estimate essentially at the outcome_008 clinical benchmark (~0.0282). Independent validation R50 gives signed difference -0.0039 with independent interval [-0.0477, 0.0400], a failure to replicate and an opposite point estimate. This is reinforced by the discordant feature_047 pattern: outcome_013 is opposite and rejected (H25), outcome_011 is null (H27), and outcome_006/outcome_014 are imprecise (H64/H65). I therefore reject H26 as a supported association and close the investigation. Overall, under the conservative scale-aware interpretation that clinically meaningful evidence requires uncertainty intervals that rule in a 10%-or-greater effect or a coherent replicated pattern, no claim is accepted. The supported finding set remains empty in this dataset. Informative negative findings include multiple intervals incompatible with clinically meaningful stronger dependency and several opposite-direction findings. Remaining uncertainty is mainly in borderline, nonreplicated, or low-precision comparisons. Next, I should allocate analysis to the strongest untested high-power registered follow-ups, especially feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 across outcomes with favorable thresholds and cells, then feature_045 outcome_008/011 extensions, before spending further validation capacity. Validation should be reserved for discovery intervals that already rule in clinically meaningful effects or for emerging multi-outcome replication, not for isolated borderline point estimates.

record.narrative: No assessment deadlines are due, so this exploration stage registers new comparisons and one reversal/refinement. The main untested priority remains feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 because it has adequate cell sizes (~578 versus ~1422) and a prior borderline stronger-dependency signal on outcome_007 (R12: signed +0.0145, below the outcome_007 threshold about 0.0245). I propose a complete feature_054 panel across the remaining outcomes, prioritizing outcomes with low scale-aware clinical thresholds and favorable variance: outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_016. These are dataset-specific association hypotheses for stronger dependency in level_002 versus level_001. Second, feature_008 is highly prevalent and has borderline prior signals on outcome_006 and outcome_014; I extend it to outcome_008, outcome_011, outcome_013, and outcome_007, which have thresholds roughly 0.0282, 0.0301, 0.0269, and 0.0245, respectively. Third, the reversed claim for feature_042 on outcome_008 is scientifically useful because the earlier stronger-dependency claim H49 was opposite: the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was positive about 0.0295, just above the outcome_008 clinical benchmark, with an interval excluding zero in that opposite direction. A new direction +1 claim asks whether this represents a clinically meaningful weaker-dependency association, though uncertainty still leaves clinical magnitude uncertain. Fourth, I register balanced interaction/subgroup comparisons using fully observed binary predictors with expected adequate four-cell counts. These avoid the sparse-subgroup problem that caused very wide intervals in prior feature_030-based interactions and test whether associations for feature_002, feature_034, or feature_054 differ by another measured predictor. Finally, I add feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_014 and outcome_006 as a limited broadening to an untested categorical predictor with a plausible level distribution. Analysis capacity should first take the strongest feature_054 and feature_008 follow-ups plus the reversed feature_042/outcome_008 candidate, then balanced interactions if main-effect capacity remains. Acceptance will require uncertainty that rules in clinically meaningful differences or coherent replicated patterns; all conclusions remain associations in this dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Study instructions:

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No validation response deadlines are open for this synthesis stage, and no new validation evidence has arrived. The current supported claim set remains empty. Under the scale-aware 10% absolute-mean benchmark, the strongest discovery candidates have not produced intervals whose lower bound rules in a clinically meaningful 10%-or-greater association, and the two prior independent validations failed to replicate the original directions. For H23, feature_042 on outcome_006 had a promising discovery estimate but independent validation reversed the point estimate. For H26, feature_047 on outcome_008 had a discovery estimate near the outcome-specific threshold, but independent validation also failed to replicate and pointed opposite. Therefore, the scientifically supported conclusion in this dataset is still absence of a confirmed clinically meaningful association. Informative negative findings include the feature_054 level_002-versus-level_001 panel across outcome_015, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_005, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_016, where intervals rule out clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and multiple binary contrasts for feature_002, feature_045, feature_034, feature_060, feature_047, and feature_042 that are near-null, opposite, or nonreplicated. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in low-threshold but interval-limited signals, especially feature_042 on outcome_014 and reversed feature_042 on outcome_008, plus feature_060 and feature_045 main effects on low-threshold outcomes. The most informative next analyses are registered here as follow-ups: complete high-value untested feature_045 lines, test feature_063 and feature_055 categorical contrasts on outcome_014 and outcome_006, and use balanced binary interactions to examine whether feature_042 or feature_060 associations differ by other fully observed predictors. Validation should remain reserved for claims that either achieve interval-level clinical magnitude or show a newly coherent multi-outcome pattern; in particular, H21 and H87 are the best future validation candidates if the pattern remains stable.

Iteration 6/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessment deadlines are due, so this stage registers refinements that ask whether the strongest remaining borderline candidates are concentrated in clinically meaningful subgroups. The feature_042 line is the best current candidate: H21 on outcome_014 is a stronger-dependency claim with signed estimate 0.0351 and 95% interval about [-0.0012, 0.0714], while H87 on outcome_008 is a reversed weaker-dependency claim with signed estimate 0.0295 and interval about [0.0055, 0.0536]. Their overall intervals still do not rule in the scale-aware 10% benchmark. I therefore test the same contrasts within balanced fully observed binary subgroups defined by feature_002, feature_034, or feature_060. If the association is concentrated in one subgroup, the subgroup lower bound could reach clinical magnitude, whereas if estimates are similar to the parent main effects or intervals remain wide, the candidate remains unsupported or can be closed. For feature_042, direction -1 on outcome_014 asks whether feature_042=1 versus 0 has a more negative score, i.e. stronger dependency, inside each subgroup. Direction +1 on outcome_008 asks whether feature_042=1 versus 0 has a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency, inside each subgroup. I add analogous refinements for H104, the reversed feature_045 outcome_014 weaker-dependency candidate, because its signed estimate 0.0218 is above the low outcome_014 benchmark but its interval includes clinically null and opposite effects. Plausible alternatives include: subgroup estimates remain nonclinical, subgroup differences arise from correlations among binary predictors, or reversed associations are artifacts of outcome-specific scaling or selection. These are dataset-specific association hypotheses; they are not causal claims. The subgroup definitions are intentionally balanced to preserve cell counts and avoid the wide intervals seen in earlier sparse feature_030 interactions.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed the twelve new discovery results using the same scale-aware clinical benchmark: a 95% signed lower bound must exceed roughly 10% of the absolute outcome mean to accept a clinically meaningful association in the claimed direction. For outcome_014 the benchmark is about 0.0093, for outcome_008 about 0.0282, and for outcome_006 about 0.0176. None of the new results reaches that interval-level acceptance rule. H106/R64 is the closest: feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_034=1 has signed estimate 0.0581 for stronger outcome_014 dependency, with lower bound 0.00916, just below the 0.0093 benchmark. It remains unresolved and active, but it is not accepted because the 95% discovery interval does not rule in the clinical threshold. H105/R63 and H107/R65 are much wider and do not add coherent evidence around this subgroup signal. For outcome_008, H108/R66 and H109/R67 are the most interesting subgroup findings: feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_002=1 and within feature_034=1 have signed estimates 0.0388 and 0.0415, respectively, above the outcome_008 benchmark, and they are consistent with the reversed main-effect H87 pattern. However, their lower bounds are 0.00338 and 0.00796, far below the benchmark, so they remain unresolved rather than accepted. H110/R68 does not support the same pattern. For feature_045 outcome_014 weaker-dependency refinements, H112/R70 gives a promising point estimate 0.0398 but a lower bound of -0.0144, while H111/R69 is near null/opposite and H113/R71 is near null; these do not provide interval-level support. H92/R72 rejects the claimed stronger-dependency direction for feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_014: the signed interval is entirely negative, corresponding to a raw weaker-dependency difference of about +0.036. Because the reversed direction still has an interval lower bound around 0.0022 after sign conversion, the opposite finding is clinically suggestive but not sufficient for acceptance. I registered a reversed proposal to keep this line explicit. H93/R73 and H98/R74 are unresolved low-threshold categorical contrasts but are not currently clinically decisive. I request no validation now: no new claim has a 95% lower bound above the relevant clinical threshold, several subgroup tests were multiplicity selected, and the feature_042 line already failed validation on outcome_006. Independent validation is better reserved for a claim that achieves interval-level clinical magnitude or a newly replicated multi-outcome direction.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered discovery results fail the acceptance rule that a 95% signed lower bound must exceed the approximately 10% absolute-mean clinical benchmark for the relevant outcome. H119, H120, H124, and H125 have point estimates that are clinically suggestive for direct weaker-dependency contrasts, but their intervals are wide and cross zero and the benchmark, so they remain unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H115-H117 are interactions; they test concentration/effect modification rather than absolute clinical magnitude and are imprecise, so they provide no independent basis for acceptance. H118 is essentially null in the claimed weaker-direction feature_063 interaction, giving no concentration signal; however, its interval still includes positive values, so I leave it unresolved but deferred rather than closed on statistical grounds. H121 and H122 are clinically informative negatives: the signed upper bounds are below the outcome_007 and outcome_015 benchmarks, and the point estimates are near null or opposite, so the claimed overall feature_063 weaker-dependency direction is not supported and those investigations are closed. H123 rejects the claimed outcome_008 weaker-dependency signal within feature_034=1 because its signed upper bound is below the outcome_008 benchmark. H103 is suggestive in the claimed stronger-direction but its point estimate is small and only the upper edge barely exceeds the benchmark; it remains unresolved and deferred, and it does not justify a new reversed weaker-direction claim. The new feature_063 results do not form a coherent multi-outcome pattern and do not concentrate the earlier reversed outcome_014 candidate H114; I therefore defer H114 rather than keep it active. I request no independent validation: no available direct mean_difference or main-effect candidate now has a discovery signed lower bound above its clinical benchmark, feature_042 and feature_002/outcome_006 candidates already failed validation, and the current feature_042/feature_063 borderline signals are too multiply selected to justify using validation before an interval-level clinical rule-in. These are dataset-specific associations only, not causal or generalizable claims.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

record.narrative: No new validation deadline or new validation result is present in this turn. The supported-findings set remains empty under the scale-aware clinical rule: a direct exposed-minus-comparator mean_difference is accepted only if its 95% signed lower bound exceeds roughly 10% of the absolute outcome mean. For the low-threshold outcomes this benchmark is about 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0175 for outcome_006, 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0245 for outcome_007, 0.0250 for outcome_015, and 0.0269 for outcome_013. The three completed independent validations have all failed to confirm their original discoveries: H23 (feature_042 on outcome_006), H26 (feature_047 on outcome_008), and H59 (feature_002 on outcome_006). These failures are not proof of no effect; they mean the available evidence does not support a generalizable clinically meaningful signal for those claims.  Current informative negative or near-negative lines include the broad feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 panel, feature_047 on outcome_008/013, feature_034 on several outcomes, feature_002 on outcome_006/013/011, and the recent feature_063 weaker-direction tests on outcome_007, outcome_015, and outcome_008 within feature_034=1. These are closed or deferred because their intervals either exclude clinically meaningful magnitudes or are too imprecise.  The main unresolved uncertainty remains around feature_042. The closest direct mean_difference near-miss is H106: outcome_014, feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_034=1, signed estimate 0.0581 and lower bound 0.00916, just below the outcome_014 benchmark. The related weaker-dependency outcome_008 subgroup estimates H108/H109 are large in point magnitude but have lower bounds far below benchmark. H114 is another near candidate: reversed feature_063 on outcome_014 has signed estimate 0.0361 but lower bound 0.0022, below benchmark. These are suggestive but not interval-supported.  For the next analyses I registered direct low-threshold tests that are most likely to produce an interpretable acceptance or informative rejection. Feature_042 overall on outcome_015, outcome_005, and outcome_007 tests whether its strong-dependency pattern is broad rather than confined to outcome_001/006/014. The feature_042 within feature_034=1 test on outcome_013 asks whether the H106 concentration also yields a clinically meaningful direct effect on another low-benchmark outcome. Feature_050 on outcome_006 and outcome_014 is motivated by the near-benchmark feature_050 signal on outcome_015; outcome_014 has a low benchmark and outcome_006 is close to the benchmark scale. Feature_052 on outcome_014 tests whether its smaller but suggestive outcome_008 effect becomes clinically meaningful on the lower-benchmark outcome_014. Finally, reversed feature_063 tests on outcome_013, outcome_001, and outcome_012 probe the remaining low-benchmark outcomes for a coherent weaker-dependency pattern after the original outcome_014 strong-direction rejection. These remain dataset-specific association hypotheses; none is a causal or mechanistic claim.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

I selected twelve direct mean_difference tests that have the best chance to either clear the scale-aware clinical benchmark or sharply narrow the current uncertainty. I therefore test feature_042 on lower-benchmark or lower-variance outcomes where the same raw effect could become interval-supported: overall outcome_015 (H126), outcome_005 (H127), outcome_007 (H128), outcome_013 within feature_034=1 (H129), and outcome_012 within feature_034=1 (H137). I also test the registered effect-modifier concentration in feature_002=0 for outcome_014 and outcome_008 (H138/H139). For the feature_063 weaker-dependency line, I prioritize H135, reversed level_002 versus level_001 on outcome_012, because its acceptance threshold is more favorable than the small-n feature_063 level_003 contrast H141 and it tests whether the raw weaker signal is coherent across outcomes. For feature_050, I request the registered feature_034=1 concentration on outcome_014 (H140) after the near-benchmark outcome_015 signal. record.narrative: The twelve new results do not provide interval-level clinical support for the claimed stronger-dependency directions under the scale-aware rule requiring a 95% signed lower bound to exceed about 10% of the absolute outcome mean. H126 and H127 reject the broad feature_042 strong-dependency hypotheses for outcome_015 and outcome_005: both signed point estimates are essentially null or opposite, and both 95% upper bounds are below the clinical benchmarks. H129 rejects feature_042 stronger dependency within feature_034=1 for outcome_013, with an opposite signed point estimate and upper bound below benchmark. H137 also rejects the claimed stronger-dependency direction for feature_042 within feature_034=1 on outcome_012; the signed interval is entirely negative. At the raw scale this is an opposite weaker-dependency signal, but the reversed lower bound would still not clear the outcome_012 benchmark, so I do not treat the post-hoc reversed direction as supported enough for acceptance or validation. H128 is a genuinely positive statistical signal for feature_042 on outcome_007, but its signed estimate 0.0195 is below the outcome_007 benchmark 0.0245 and its interval extends above the benchmark; therefore the claim remains unresolved rather than clinically accepted. The remaining new results are underpowered or too imprecise: H135 feature_063 on outcome_012 is suggestive but below benchmark; H138/H139 are small subgroup-restricted feature_042 estimates with wide intervals; H140 feature_050 within feature_034=1, H142 feature_048 level_001 versus level_003, and H144 feature_032 on outcome_014 are wide despite suggestive points; and H143 feature_048 level_002 versus level_003 has only 25 exposed observations and is too unstable to pursue. The strongest new point estimate is H144: rare feature_032 associated with substantially stronger outcome_014 dependency, signed estimate 0.0685, but the 95% interval crosses zero and multiplicity/subgroup selection caution applies. I do not request validation now because validation-adjusted intervals are stricter and the current candidates either cross zero, are subgroup-selected, or are small-cell estimates unlikely to survive independent adjusted intervals. I propose low-variance outcome follow-ups for feature_032 because if H144 reflects a genuine broad dependency association rather than outcome_014-specific noise or outlier-driven rare-exposure noise, it should be clearer on lower-variance outcomes with comparable clinical thresholds. Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The new validation evidence for H57 and the overdue validation response for H59 both fail to support clinically meaningful dependency-score differences under the scale-aware rule that a direct signed lower bound should exceed roughly 10% of the absolute outcome mean. For H59, feature_002 on outcome_006 has discovery signed estimate +0.0209 with 95% interval -0.0139 to +0.0556 and outcome_006 benchmark about 0.0175. The independent validation estimate is +0.0041 with a stricter validation interval -0.0462 to +0.0545. The validation point estimate is near null and its lower bound is below zero, so it does not confirm the original discovery. I maintain rejection and close the investigation: the available evidence does not support a clinically meaningful feature_002 association with outcome_006 in this dataset, although this is not proof of no effect. For H57, feature_060 on outcome_008 has discovery signed estimate +0.0064 with 95% interval -0.0151 to +0.0280, already below the outcome_008 benchmark about 0.0282. The independent validation signed estimate is only +0.0081 with stricter interval -0.0233 to +0.0395. Although the strict interval upper edge includes the benchmark, the independent point estimate is very small, about 3% of the absolute outcome mean, and the lower bound is far below the benchmark. Combined with the small discovery estimate, there is no interval-supported clinically meaningful association; I reject the H57 stronger-dependency claim and close it. The overall supported-findings set remains empty. Completed validations H23, H26, H57, and H59 all failed to confirm their original discovery directions, strengthening caution about early borderline signals. The most scientifically informative unresolved line is now the rare feature_032 candidate on outcome_014 (H144), which has a large point estimate but a wide interval crossing zero; the registered follow-ups on lower-variance outcomes H146, H147, and H148 are the best next tests for whether this is a broad association or outcome_014-specific noise. Feature_042 remains a near/borderline but inconsistent line: H106 is barely below benchmark, H128 is statistically positive but below outcome_007 benchmark, and other feature_042 tests are null or opposite. I would not request validation for those borderline, multiply selected near misses unless a new interval-level clinical rule-in appears. These conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.
